title: Slot fractionation minute-surge sampler memo
content:
Short summary:

This note describes a targeted microbenchmark (the "surge sampler") designed to evaluate minute-scale surge patterns under different slot fractionation strategies. Goal: quantify p50/p90/p99 latency and incremental $/1k-queries for 60s surge windows across three slotization policies (no-fraction, quarter-slot, micro-slot) and two cache hit regimes (cold-first, warmed-prefetch). This is a working brief with raw ascii charts + interpretation for engineering/product tradeoffs.

Background and why this is unique:
- Many prior artifacts looked at sustained bursts or long-running microbursts; we wanted data on minute-length surges typical of marketing pushes or notification storms.
- "Slot fractionation" refers to splitting a GPU allocation slot into multiple smaller time-slices to better absorb short surges while keeping steady-state efficiency. Quarter-slot: up to 4 logical slots per physical slot. Micro-slot: up to 8.

Environment and test harness:
- runtime: redwood-runtime v2.7.3 with slotization feature-flag (enable-slot-fractionation=true)
- hardware: p4d-ish hosts (A100-40GB equivalent); tests repeated on NVIDIA Ampere and one small test on older V100 nodes to sanity-check regressions
- workload generator: surge-sampler v0.9 (internal), 60s ramp: 0->350 qps in 10s, sustain 60s, decay 10s, baseline 5 qps.
- model: open-llama-7b-instr (sequence 128 prompt + 64 gen) at FP16; same model compiled with quant-4 for a separate sweep (results below focus on FP16).
- cache regimes: "cold-first" (no KV cache primed) and "prefetch-warm" (top 10% session prefixes primed).
- measurement: per-request observed latency at client (end-to-end), cost proxy = amortized GPU-seconds converted to $/1k-queries using internal unit rates.

Test matrix (selected):
- Policies: no-fraction (baseline), quarter-slot, micro-slot
- Concurrency targets: slot cap set so baseline sustains 30qps; surge pushes up to 350qps transiently
- Repeats: 6 runs per cell; median of medians used for charts.

Raw result sketches (median across runs) — latency percentiles vs policy (cold-first):

Policy        | p50 (ms) | p90 (ms) | p99 (ms) | delta $/1k
--------------|----------|----------|----------|-----------
no-fraction   | 68       | 210      | 940      | +$4.8
quarter-slot   | 82       | 160      | 420      | +$2.1
micro-slot     | 95       | 130      | 245      | +$1.6

Observations: fractionation reduces tail dramatically at the cost of modest p50 increases and extra scheduling overhead -> measured as incremental $/1k. For cold-first runs the micro-slot policy reduces p99 by ~740ms vs baseline while adding ~$1.6/1k.

Warm-prefetch regime (same table):

Policy        | p50 (ms) | p90 (ms) | p99 (ms) | delta $/1k
--------------|----------|----------|----------|-----------
no-fraction   | 44       | 112      | 230      | +$2.0
quarter-slot   | 49       | 98       | 160      | +$1.1
micro-slot     | 55       | 86       | 118      | +$0.9

Observations: when prefetching/kvcache is effective, slot fractionation still reduces tails but margins tighten — baseline already performs well; micro-slot adds marginal cost but gives best p99.

Minute-scale latency timeline (ascii sparkline) — example run (micro-slot, warm-prefetch):
- qps timeline (short):  [5, 12, ▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓ 350, 350, 350, 350, 180, 70, 20, 5]
- p99 ms timeline:        [60, 65, 70, 88, 95, 110, 120, 130, 100, 85, 70, 60]
- ascii bar (p99):        |▁▁▁▁▁▂▂▃▃▃▂▁

Cost-per-1k heatmap (delta over baseline) — rows=policy, cols=window slice:
- window slices: pre-surge (t-30 to t0), ramp (0-10s), sustain (10-70s), decay (70-80s), tail (80-120s)

no-fraction:   [+$0.1, +$0.9, +$4.8, +$1.0, +$0.2]
quarter-slot:  [+$0.2, +$0.6, +$2.1, +$0.5, +$0.1]
micro-slot:    [+$0.3, +$0.5, +$1.6, +$0.4, +$0.1]

Interpretation and tradeoffs:
1) Tail protection vs steady-state efficiency
   - Micro-slot does best at short surges: reduces p99 by 3-4x vs no-fraction in cold scenarios. This is valuable for customer-facing features where p99 user-perceived latency matters (chat UIs, assistant calls).
   - But micro-slot increases baseline scheduling overhead and slightly higher p50 due to smaller time-slices and more context switches. The measured p50 uplift (~20–30ms) is usually imperceptible compared to p99 benefits during surges.

2) Cache priming synergy
   - Prefetching/KV-caching reduces the incremental value of fractionation; if product can reliably prime hot prefixes, simpler slot policies are cost-effective.

3) Cost per 1k — when to enable globally vs on-demand
   - If a customer has <= 5 short surges/day, global micro-slot yields marginal incremental cost but consistent tail protection.
   - For heavy-surge customers, quarter-slot or hybrid policies (adaptive fractionation only during observed QPS slope > X) are recommended to cap unit costs.

Operational notes and potential failure modes:
- Fragmentation: extreme micro-slotting can lead to fragmentation where scheduler leaves tiny unused gaps — observed on one V100 host; add defrag heuristics or cap micro-slot when host load > 80%.
- Cold start: cold-first scenarios show the largest delta; ensure prewarming or KV prefetch for high-priority tenants.
- Telemetry: add per-slot missed-fill metrics and cross-check with client-observed p99 to avoid mismatches.

Recommended next experiments:
- Repeat same matrix with quantized models (q4) and larger sequence lengths (512) to see scaling of tail benefits.
- Adaptive policy A/B: enable fractionation only when dQPS/dt > 20 qps/s and measure cost delta over 30 days with synthetic spikes + real traffic replay.
- Run long tail exposure test: 10k simulated short surges/day across 100 tenants to validate fragmentation heuristics.

Appendix — raw numeric excerpt (median of medians):
- no-fraction (cold): p50=68, p90=210, p99=940, cost_delta_per_1k=4.8
- quarter-slot (cold): p50=82, p90=160, p99=420, cost_delta_per_1k=2.1
- micro-slot (cold): p50=95, p90=130, p99=245, cost_delta_per_1k=1.6
- no-fraction (warm): p50=44, p90=112, p99=230, cost_delta_per_1k=2.0
- quarter-slot (warm): p50=49, p90=98, p99=160, cost_delta_per_1k=1.1
- micro-slot (warm): p50=55, p90=86, p99=118, cost_delta_per_1k=0.9

Commands & artifacts to reproduce (notes):
- harness repo: github.com/redwood-inference/surge-sampler (branch: slot-fractionation-experiments)
- to run locally (example):
  ./surge-sampler --model open-llama-7b-instr --policy micro-slot --cache warm --runs 6 --qps-peak 350 --seq 192 > run-microslot-warm.log
- result parsing: tools/parse-surges.py --input run-*.log --out summary.json

Open questions / decisions:
- Default policy for hosted-tier-1: keep no-fraction or switch to quarter-slot? Proposal: ship quarter-slot as default for tier-1 (gives good tail reduction with limited cost), gate micro-slot behind a feature flag for latency-sensitive customers. Decision needed from product (product@) by EOD 2028-04-12.

If you'd like, I can produce the same brief but with combined per-tenant cost projection over a 30-day synthetic load (90th percentile customer scenarios).

-- Aisha
